label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
Hi Mikaela, sorry it’s taken me a bit to give you a proper answer. You helped us heaps when Dave did his shoulder so I owe you more than “yep going good”!

We’ve got 290 cows, mostly 3-way crossbreds, and started on 21 September after mating had started. We skip Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday afternoon milkings, so four once-a-days a week. Mornings are still 5.15 every day, no sleep-ins unfortunately.

Going off the Fonterra app we’re down about 6% on milksolids for the same weeks last year. That’s just our comparison, not saying all of that is the milking change or that yours would be the same. The rep had told us to expect 8–10%, so it hasn’t been as bad as we’d braced for. But 6% is still milk we’re not getting paid for, I won’t pretend otherwise.

Cells did jump. We were about 110,000 and went up to around 180,000 in the first three weeks. Back around 135,000 now. So not mental, but enough to have me watching them pretty closely.

The worst bit was a heifer with mastitis that went bad on a skipped afternoon. We didn’t spot her till the next morning and she lost a quarter. That’s the bit I’d want you to hear as well as all the nice things about afternoons off. You really do have to be on your game with teat spraying and checking cows on the skip days. Not going through the shed doesn’t mean you can forget about them till morning, or it bites you.

The cows settled quicker than I expected. About four days of bellowing at the gate and then they seemed to accept the new arrangement better than I did!

Lameness is way down. Four on the lame list now compared with 11 this time last year. Our back paddocks are a 1.8km walk, so cutting some of those trips out is a fair saving on their feet.

For us the biggest difference has been the people. First skipped Sunday afternoon, Dave and I went to Hamilton to see the grandkids. First Sunday afternoon off in spring in twenty-odd years. Felt very odd leaving, but lovely once we got there. Kieran said it’s the first spring he hasn’t wanted to quit by October. That probably tells you more about the hours than I can.

Honestly, I wouldn’t go back. For us the hours alone are worth the 6%. If Tom’s knees are that bad I reckon the afternoons off would help him more than anything, and I can understand why you’re looking at it with your young fella too.

But we started in September, so I can only tell you how it’s gone here so far. I can’t promise what starting after Christmas would look like for you, or what you’d be saying about it in March. There’s a real production cost and that mastitis heifer was a hard lesson.

Come and have a look through our shed rosters and numbers with me at the field day on the 19th. Happy to show you the actual figures, warts and all. Or just ring me whenever suits. Much easier than texting with these useless thumbs!
